base_qualification.rule: P1 work is additive relative to this exact qualified B0 evidence point. No pre-existing file may be modified, deleted, or renamed.

purpose: Add a local grounding proof kind for regression witnesses over multi-world K1 claims. One independently checked observed forbidden pair may prove regression without closing, modeling, or fabricating unrelated worlds.

semantic_non_change.breaking_rule: One grounded realized pair outside ALLOW is sufficient for REGRESSION.
semantic_non_change.preservation_rule: Unchanged. P1 has zero preservation authority and cannot discharge closure, totality, or global inclusion obligations.

identity.implementation_id: impl:sha256 of exact executable bytes supplied independently to the checker
identity.target_commitment_rule: target_id commits to profile, claim_id, pair, implementation_id, SHA-256 of exact world-input bytes, SHA-256 of exact effect-log bytes, selected record index, timeout flag, exit code, stdout SHA-256, and stderr SHA-256 using domain-separated length-prefixed transcript encoding.

grounding_algorithm: Strictly validate the W0 claim and regression witness, including claim_id and witness_id recomputation.
Require witness.grounding_proof.kind == k1.observed-pair/v1 and exact proof-artifact byte digest equality.
Reject if the witness pair world is not declared by the claim or if the pair is already in ALLOW.
Strictly parse the proof artifact; unknown profile is UNSUPPORTED, not accepted.
Require artifact claim_id and pair to equal the witness claim_id and pair.
Decode base64 canonically. Recompute world ID from exact world_input bytes and require it equals pair.world.
Strictly parse E1 effect-sink records. record_index must name an existing exact record. Recompute that record's consequence commitment and require it equals pair.consequence.
Hash the independently supplied executable bytes and require exact equality with artifact.implementation_id.
Recompute the observed-pair target commitment and require artifact.target_id and witness.target_id to match it.
Only then return ACCEPTED/REGRESSION with scope LOCAL_OBSERVED_PAIR and preservation_authority=false.

establishes: The submitted W0 claim admits the witness world.
The selected consequence is not allowed in that world.
The exact embedded observation bytes encode the submitted pair under the recognized observation profile.
The artifact is content-bound to the exact executable bytes supplied to the checker.
No evidence or closure for unrelated claim worlds is required for regression.
does_not_establish: Preservation from any number of clean runs.
That embedded observation bytes were causally produced by the executable outside a controlled binding runner.
Authenticated remote attestation, signature, or transferable trust.
Anything about unobserved worlds beyond claim membership and ALLOW commitments.

vectors: three-world claim; grounded forbidden pair in one world
pair world not declared by claim
selected record index out of range
observed-pair proof used as preservation authority
unrelated worlds have no local observations
reorder claim worlds and ALLOW without semantic change
multiple effect records; selected forbidden record grounded
timeout/nonzero metadata after durable forbidden record

independence_requirement.checker_a: Python standard library only; must not import W1/W2/B0 binder code.
independence_requirement.checker_b: Go standard library only; must not execute Python or import RISU checker code.
independence_requirement.differential_rule: Both checkers must independently recompute claim identity, witness identity, artifact byte digest, world/effect commitments, executable digest, target commitment, and final authority class.

binding_follow_on.name: B1 multi-world local binding
binding_follow_on.rule: A controlled runner may mint a P1 artifact only from an actual effect sink it observed. Clean/no-forbidden runs mint no regression witness and acquire no preservation authority.

stop_rule: If any adversarial vector or cross-language differential exposes an ambiguity that can change authority, stop and amend the prospective protocol before qualification. Do not waive a failed vector to preserve the design.
